Preserve SASRec through an additive branch, h′=h+α·g(h,p)·p, with α initialized to zero; a sigmoid gate initialized at zero outputs 0.5 and does not preserve the baseline. Keep existing normalization and scoring unchanged; avoid adding LayerNorm after the residual. This follows [ReZero’s identity initialization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887). Normalize embeddings for cosine weights only, while pooling values on a scale compatible with SASRec features; raw item embeddings, √d-scaled inputs, and normalized hidden states are not interchangeable. Explicitly mask padding in similarities, values, denominators, and outputs; return zero for empty prefixes. [PyTorch padding_idx](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Embedding) protects lookup gradients, not every subsequent operation.

Implementation synthesis: at training position t, compute recurrence exclusively from valid items j≤t; exclude the next-item target. A full-sequence similarity statistic broadcast backward leaks future information. Define whether self-similarity counts: the diagonal contributes a constant one and can dominate short prefixes. Specify the cosine kernel explicitly; signed cosine sums can cancel, so normalized pooling needs a nonnegative kernel or another stable denominator. For truncated length L and dimension d, pairwise cosine recurrence costs O(BL²d) time and O(BL²) similarity storage. Sliding-window pooling costs O(BLKd), or O(BLd) for suitable running sums. Exact factorable kernels permit prefix accumulators, but arbitrary clipping/softmax does not inherit [linear attention’s recurrence](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/katharopoulos20a.html).

Recommended controls, rather than established results for this exact extension: compare unchanged SASRec, scale/normalization-only, recency-only pooling, cosine recurrence, and popularity-controlled recurrence. Hold gates, windows, initialization, optimizer, and validation candidates fixed. Estimate popularity from training interactions only; use frequency-matched comparisons or explicitly defined frequency correction. These isolate similarity effects from recency, embedding norms, and popular-item concentration.
